content.thinking:
Two feature flags flipped at the same time, so I need to work out which one is actually behind the error. The failure sits in spend_summary.py, which points at monthly-spend-feature being on, but legacy-checkout-fallback being off also sends traffic to the new renderer, and that renderer is the one calling the spend summary. At 18:15 the traffic split shows legacy-off at 152 against 48 on, and spend-on at 153 against 47 off, so the two changes overlap almost completely and I can't yet tell them apart.

I'm weighing whether the monthly-spend flag or the legacy-checkout fallback is the real trigger, since they move in near-lockstep at 18:15. The error traces to spend_summary.py, which points at monthly-spend-feature, though I can't yet rule out the renderer path. I'm leaning toward monthly-spend-feature as the cause, at roughly 0.6 confidence.

input.reason: legacy-checkout-fallback did switch off at 18:15:13Z, but monthly-spend-feature was switched on at the same instant and the errors are ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47, which points at the spend feature. The two flags moved in lockstep, so the logs cannot separate them.
